Condition : 3 - Flood Risk Assessment
The proposed development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Flood Risk Assessment (Assessment Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre Risk Assessment, revision 1, dated 12 July, project number 60668255, prepared by AECOM) and the following mitigation measures it details, including:

Finished floor levels shall be set no lower than 6.33m above Ordnance Datum. This mitigation measure shall be fully implemented prior to occupation and subsequently in accordance with the scheme's timing/phasing arrangements. The measures detailed above shall be retained and maintained thereafter throughout the lifetime of development.
Reason: To reduce the risk of flooding to the proposed development and future occupants
Condition : 4 - Details of diversion of water asset	
Any works to the proposed diverted watercourse should be undertaken in accordance with the Ordinary Watercourse Consent issued by the Lead Local Flood Authority dated 25th March 2024 and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 24th April 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/1003, unless otherwise agreed in writing between the Lead Local Flood Authority and the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To reduce the risk of flooding to the proposed development and future occupants. 

Supporting information: The applicant should do so by completing an Ordinary Watercourse Consent Application Form. For further information and guidance, please email: flooding@hounslow.gov.uk. The applicant should also confirm as part of the discharge of this condition if they have consulted Thames Water with regards to this application.
Condition : 5 - Construction Environment Management Plan
The proposed development will be constructed in line with the approved Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) prepared by RPS (document reference JNY11669- 01a CEMP Version 01a dated 08 December 2023) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 8th March 2025 under condition discharge application P/2023/3926, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to safeguard the amenities of adjoining residents and the amenities of the locality 
Condition : 6 - Demolition Management Plan	
Any demolition proposed will be undertaken in line with the approved Demolition Management Plan prepared by Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust (document reference Rev B), as approved by the Local Planning Authority on 18 March 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/0104 unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure highway safety is maintained and preserved and in the interests of air quality and neighbour amenity 
Condition : 7 - Construction Logistics Plan	
The proposed development will be constructed in line with the approved Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) prepared by RPS (document reference 794-PLN-TRP-JNY11669-02d CLP Version 02d dated 14 January 2025) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 29 April 2025 under condition discharge application P/2025/0107, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure highway safety is maintained and preserved and in the interests of air quality and neighbour amenity 
Condition : 8 - Contamination
The proposed development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Phase 1 Geo-Environmental Preliminary Risk Assessment prepared by RPS (Reference: JER9223, dated 6 September 2021) approved under application P2022/2424, and the Geotechnical and Geo-Environmental Interpretative Report prepared by AECOM (Reference: P01), approved by the Local Planning Authority on 5 March 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/0110.

For the avoidance of doubt, the requirements of Parts (a) and (b) of the contamination condition have been discharged. The following requirements shall continue to apply during the course of development:


During the course of the development:

The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if additional contamination is discovered during the course of the development. A competent person shall assess the additional contamination, and shall submit appropriate amendments to the scheme for decontamination in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval before any work on that aspect of development continues.

Before the development is first brought into use:

a)	The agreed scheme for decontamination referred to in clauses b) and c) above, including amendments, shall be fully implemented and a written validation (closure) report submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. The LPA therefore wishes to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety
Condition : 9 - Archaeology	
All development shall be undertaken in accordance with the Written Scheme of Investigation Stage 1 prepared by KJS Heritage (document reference KJSHWMH1023 dated 8 September 2023) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 5 March 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/0144, and the Written Scheme of Investigation Stage 2 prepared by Wessex Archaeology (document reference 288181.03 dated September 2024) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 17 January 2025 under condition discharge application P/2024/3160, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to safeguard the site in terms of its archaeological interest 
Condition : 10 - Revised Air Quality Assessment	
The proposed development will be constructed in line with the approved Air Quality Assessment prepared by Stroma (document reference PRO-063832 dated January 2024) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 26 March 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/0337 (discharging conditions 10 and 11), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to ensure that the future users of the development will not be exposed to a significant increase in poor air quality
Condition : 11 - Air Quality Neutral Assessment	
The proposed development will be constructed in line with the approved Air Quality Assessment prepared by Stroma (document reference PRO-063832 dated January 2024) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 26 March 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/0337 (discharging conditions 10 and 11), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to ensure that the future users of the development will not be exposed to a significant increase in poor air quality

Condition : 12 - Ecological Management Plan	
The ecological mitigation, enhancement and management measures detailed in the Ecological Management Plan prepared by Lizard Landscaping (document reference LLD2417-ECO-REP-004-05-EDS dated 31 March 2026), as approved under planning permission P/2024/4276, shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 

Where the proposals submitted as part of Phase 2 depart from the approved Ecological Management Plan, an updated Ecological Mitigation, Enhancement and Management Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of Phase 2. The updated strategy shall demonstrate that the proposed changes would result in no adverse ecological impacts compared with the approved scheme. The approved measures, including any subsequently approved amendments, shall thereafter be implemented, retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: In order to ensure that the future users of the development will not be exposed to a significant increase in poor air quality

Condition : 13 - Drainage Strategy	
The proposed development shall be delivered in accordance with the details approved under discharge of condition application P/2024/0550, approved on 24 April 2024, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
For the avoidance of doubt, only Part A of the condition has been discharged. The requirements of Part B shall remain in force and shall be carried out in accordance with the original wording of the planning condition.

A.	Prior to commencement of the development excluding site investigations and demolition), and notwithstanding the approved details, the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations and an updated Drainage Assessment Form to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the Flood Risk Assessment (12/07/2022), and associated drawings. It must be demonstrated that the site will not flood as a result of the 1 in 30 year rainfall event, that there will be no flooding of buildings as a result of events up to and including the 1 in 100 year rainfall event, and on-site flow as a result the 1 in 100 year event with a climate change consideration must be suitably managed. Runoff rates and attenuation volumes should align across all documents provided. It should be shown that rainwater harvesting techniques and green infrastructure have been considered within the design. Consent from Thames Water must be provided demonstrating there is sufficient capacity in their network for the proposed discharge rate. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of development.
B.	The proposed development shall not be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme has been completed in accordance with the submitted det
Condition : 14 - Heat Pumps (GSHP) and Air Source Heat Pumps (ASHP)
The air source heat pumps shall be installed and operated in accordance with the approved details provided as part of application P/2025/1519 approved on 24 June 2025.

Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards 
Condition : 15 - Bird Hazard Management Plan	
The proposed development will be constructed in line with the approved Bird Hazard Management Plan prepared by Greengage (document reference 552726JB14MAR24DV01_BHMP dated March 2024) and approved by the Local Planning Authority on 24 April 2024 under condition discharge application P/2024/0932, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: It is necessary to manage the flat roofs to minimise its attractiveness to birds which could endanger the safe movement of aircraft and e operation of Heathrow Airport. 
Information:
The BHMP must ensure that flat/shallow pitched roofs be constructed to allow access to all areas by foot using permanent fixed access stairs ladders or similar. The owner/occupier must not allow gulls, to nest, roost or loaf on the building. Checks must be made weekly or sooner if bird activity dictates, during the breeding season. Outside of the breeding season gull activity must be monitored and the roof checked regularly to ensure that gulls do not utilise the roof. Any gulls found nesting, roosting or loafing must be dispersed by the owner/occupier when detected or when requested by Heathrow Airside Operations staff. In some instances, it may be necessary to contact Heathrow Airside Operations staff before bird dispersal takes place. The owner/occupier must remove any nests or eggs found on the roof. The breeding season for gulls typically runs from March to June. The owner/occupier must obtain the appropriate licences where applicable from Natural England before the removal of nests and eggs.
Condition : 16 - Details of external materials
The proposed development will be constructed in accordance with the approved materials provided under application P/2024/2787 approved on 1 October 2024.

Reason: In order that the Council may be satisfied as to the details of the development in the interests of the visual amenity of the area 
Condition : 17 - BREEAM Interim
A BREEAM New Construction Fully Fitted Assessment has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The developer has demonstrated that the development will achieve an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits. This has been confirmed under condition discharge application P/2026/0978, approved on 26 March 2026.
For the avoidance of doubt, Part A of the original condition has been discharged under application P/2026/0978. Part B of the condition remains in force and shall be complied with in accordance with the requirements of the original planning condition.
The proposed development, unless otherwise agreed in writing, shall achieve an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits under BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) for the BREEAM New Construction Fully Fitted Assessment.
A. Prior to the occupation of the development, a BREEAM New Construction Fully Fitted Assessment shall be submitted, by the developer, and approved in writing by the local planning authority to demonstrate how the development will achieve an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits.
B. Within 6 months of the completion of Phase 2 of the development, unless otherwise agreed in writing, a BREEAM New Construction Fully Fitted (Post Construction) Certificate, issued by
the BRE (or equivalent accredited body), must be submitted by the developer, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that an 'Excellent' rating and all mandatory BREEAM 'Excellent' credits. All the measures integrated shall be retained for as long as the development is in existence.

Reason: To ensure a sustainable development

Condition : 18 - BREEAM completion

This planning condition was deleted by application P/2026/0269. No further action required.
Condition : 19 - Sustainable sourcing	of materials	
The proposed development will be constructed in accordance with the details approved under P/2024/2514 dated 30 October 2024.
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials 

Condition : 20 - Landscaping
The landscaping proposals for Phase 1 shall be delivered in accordance with the details approved under condition discharge application P/2025/0713, approved on 4 June 2025, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
For the avoidance of doubt, Part A of the original condition has been discharged in respect of the Phase 1 landscaping details approved under application P/2025/0713. The requirements of Part B, together with the approved implementation, management, maintenance and replacement provisions of the original condition, shall continue to apply and be carried out in accordance with the original condition wording.
A.	Within 6 months of above ground works commencing of the development, and notwithstanding the submitted plans, full details of both hard and soft landscape works for both Phase 1 and 2 of landscaping shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
i.	The works identified in areas within Phase 1 on Plan Number ADC-ACM-XX-00-DR- AR-100113 P07, shall then be carried out as approved prior to the occupation of the development and maintained as such at all times thereafter.
ii.	Works to areas identified within Phase 2 on Plan Number ADC-ACM-XX-00-DR-AR- 100113 P07 shall then be carried out as approved within 6 months of occupation of the development, and maintained as such at all times thereafter.
The details shall include (surface treatments; proposed finished levels or contours; means of enclosure; car parking layouts; other vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas and footways; hard surfacing materials; minor artefacts and structures (eg. furniture); lighting; signs; proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (eg drainage power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating lines, manholes, supports etc.); and boundary treatments).
Details of the soft landscape works shall include (planting plans; written specifications (including cultivation a
Condition : 21 - Details of external lighting
The Phase 1 external lighting strategy shall be delivered in accordance with the details approved under condition discharge application P/2025/0714 dated 4th June 2025, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Within 6 months of the above ground works commencing for the development of phase 2, a phase-specific lighting strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These documents shall explain:
�	Any lighting proposed for external communal areas;
�	The proposed external building lighting;
�	Confirmation that lighting will achieve the standards in BS 5489;
�	Details of measures to adequately mitigate light pollution affecting neighbouring residential properties and ecology.
The strategy shall accord with the Code of Practice for the Reduction of Light Pollution (2021) issued by the Institute of Lighting Engineers. The approved mitigation measures shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Reason: To ensure the development is adequately lit in order to minimise the risk and fear of crime, whilst ensuring that the proposed lighting would not unduly impact on local character, amenity or biodiversity
Condition : 22 - Cycle parking and associated infrastructure
Prior to completion of Phase 2 of the development, and notwithstanding the submitted plans, full details including the number (minimum of 20 spaces), location, the design (plans, elevations and sections) of secure structures and manufacturer's specifications) of all cycle stands for the staff of, and visitors to, the development including any additional infrastructure such as repair/maintenance stands and equipment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
� The Short Stay Cycle Parking will be delivered as part of Phase 1;
� The Long Stay Cycle Parking, as approved under planning permission P/2026/1294, will be delivered as part of Phase 2.
� The overall cycle parking should have 20% of single -tier Sheffield stands and 5% enlarged spaces.  
� A minimum spacing of 0.4 metres between two-tier cycle parking stands
(c) details of cycle parking security measures;
(d) details of CCTV and access control arrangements.
The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use following completion of the relevant phases before the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: To ensure the provision of high quality, safe and accessible cycle parking facilities 
Condition : 23 - EV charging points	
Prior to occupation of the development, full details of the Electric Vehicle Charging Points, each capable of a minimum output of 7.2kW, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the number, location, and manufacturer's specifications.
The charging points shall be installed within 6 months of the occupation of the development and in accordance with the approved details and so maintained at all times thereafter.

Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport
Condition : 24 - 'Be  Seen'  energy
monitoring	A. The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy. �
B. Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions, and achieved 28% reduction in emissions.
C. Upon final commencement of operation of any low and zero carbon technologies, suitable monitoring devices for the monitoring of the low and zero carbon technologies shall have been installed, and the monitored data shall be submitted automatically to a monitoring web platform at daily intervals for a period of three years from the point of full operation and be made available to the local planning authority on request for a period of five years.

Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions 

Condition : 25 - Signposting for People with Disabilities	
Prior to occupation of the development, sign plates, incorporating a representation of the Universal Wheelchair Symbol, should be displayed to indicate the location of convenient facilities to meet the needs of people with disabilities. Such sign plates should identify or advertise accessible entrances to buildings, reserved parking spaces, accessible lifts and lavatory accommodation, manageable routes through buildings and availability of special services. Signs for direction and location should have large characters or numerals and clearly contrast with the background colour. Thereafter, these features shall be retained and maintained for the life of the development.
Reason: To ensure that people with disabilities are aware of the location of convenient facilities
Condition : 26 - Implementation	of car parking	
Within 6 months of the first occupation of the development, the car parking shown on the approved plans under P/2026/1294 shall be installed on the site and so maintained at all times thereafter in accordance with the Parking Management Plan (PMP) (Condition 29).
The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until the replacement parking, cycle parking, pedestrian access and associated works approved under planning permission P/2026/1294 have been implemented in full and made available for use.

Reason: To ensure the scheme does not give rise to highway safety concerns and accords with the aims and objectives of the Council's sustainable transport agenda

Condition : 27 - Delivery and Service Management Plan	
The proposed development will be constructed in line with the approved Delivery and Servicing Plan prepared by SLR (document reference 425.068006.00001 01 dated 22 April 2026).

Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives

Condition : 28 - Parking provided and retained	
Condition 28 is deleted as it duplicates the requirements of Condition 26, which has already been imposed.
Condition : 29 - Parking Management Plan	
The proposed development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Car Park Management Plan prepared by SLR (Document Reference 425.068006.00001 01, dated 22 April 2026), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The approved parking areas shall thereafter be operated, managed and maintained in accordance with the approved Car Park Management Plan for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport and safeguard the amenities of surrounding residential properties and ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality
Condition : 30 - Details of oil interceptors	
The petrol/oil interceptors shall be installed in accordance with the details approved under condition discharge application P/2026/1051 approved on 29 May 2026, prior to the occupation of each phase of the development and retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the local planning authority.
Reason: To enforce the effective use of petrol/oil interceptors so that the development shall not result in oil-polluted discharges entering local watercourses 
Condition : 31 - Secure by Design	
The development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO) following the principles of the Secured by Design Hospital Guide, which can be found at: www.securedbydesign.com/guidance/designguides.
The development shall not be occupied until accreditation has been achieved and evidence of such accreditation has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 to consider crime and disorder implications in excising its planning functions; to promote the well- being of the area in pursuance of the Council's powers under section 2 of the Local Government Act 2000 and to ensure the development provides a safe and secure environment

Condition : 32 - Closed Circuit Television 
Prior to occupation of the relevant phase of the development, a scheme for the provision of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Metropolitan Police. The scheme for the provision of CCTV shall include the following:
�	Details of CCTV cameras;
�	Details of the location of CCTV cameras to be mounted on and/or around or within the buildings, amenity areas and bicycle storage areas.
Prior to occupation of Phase 1 of the development, the development shall be completed in accordance with the details approved under condition discharge application P/2026/1186 on 26 June 2026 and thereafter maintained for the life of the development. Unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In the interests of safety and security 
Condition : 33 - Secure Access
Prior to the occupation of the development, details for the design of an electronic access control system that is capable of securing the communal and public areas shall be submitted and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Metropolitan Police. Details shall include:
�	A dynamic lockdown system capable of securing areas with little notice
�	A dynamic lockdown procedure incorporating the open source, Home Office 'Run Hide Tell' guidance and tested and exercised regularly;
�	How entry and exit points can be secured quickly, providing robust doors (in accordance with DOCO/Secured by Design advice) on all entrances that can be locked by the activation of a single control from the reception area and security office.
�	Where possible, final exit fire escape doors to be 'fail safe and secure' subject to compliance with Fire Safety regulations;
�	The electronic access control system must also secure the staff only roof terrace to prevent unauthorised access;
�	'No Drone Zone' signage must clearly be displayed in all outdoor areas, including the roof terrace

Reason: In the interests of safety and security

Condition : 34 - Restrictive use of hospital	
The proposed development shall be used as a hospital for the provision of medical and health services and no other purpose including any other purposes in Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification.
Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby approved would not result in detriment to adjoining properties but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Class in the interests of amenity and the protection of critical public health infrastructure
Condition : 35 - Internal noise criteria
Noise outside the buildings shall be controlled to allow the internal noise criteria in sensitive spaces to be achieved (with windows or trickle vents open for ventilation if the space is naturally ventilated) in accordance with Table 1 of HTM-08-1 'Criteria for noise intrusion from external sources.'
Prior to occupation of the development and upon installation of the proposed fixed plant and any associated mitigation, an acoustic commissioning survey shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To ensure that the future staff and visitors of the development do not suffer an unreasonable level of noise and disturbance

Condition : 36 - Fixed plant noise restriction	
The cumulative noise from any fixed external plant associated with the scheme should not exceed levels more than 10 dB below representative background (LA90) levels at free field locations representing facades of nearby existing and proposed dwellings. Noise levels should be assessed by measurement or calculation based on the guidance presented within BS4142: 2014+A1:2019 or subsequent versions of this guidance and where appropriate, mitigation measures to achieve the specified criteria should be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In addition, noise levels from fixed plant should not exceed 50dB LAeq,T within the boundary of Isleworth Cemetery.
Prior to occupation of the development and upon installation of the proposed fixed plant and any associated mitigation, an acoustic commissioning survey shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To ensure that the future staff and visitors of the development and neighbouring sensitive uses do not suffer an unreasonable level of noise and disturbance 
Condition : 37 - Hours of construction	
No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00 am to 6:00 pm on Mondays to Fridays and 8:00 am to 1:00 pm on Saturdays, and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority. Daytime works will not exceed 75 dB LAeq,T at the worst affected residential property during the above time periods.

Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the amenities of the locality

Condition : 38 - Air Quality � NRMM	
All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) used during the course of the development that is within the scope of the GLA 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance (SPG) dated July 2014, or any successor document, shall comply with the emissions requirements therein.
Reason: In the interests of air quality 

Condition : 39 - Tree retention	
In this condition 'retained tree' means any existing tree which is to be retained in accordance with the approved plans and particulars, and paragraphs (a) and (b) below shall have effect until the expiration of five years from the date of the occupation of any of the buildings hereby approved.
a. No retained tree shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any retained tree be topped or lopped other than in accordance with the approved plans and particulars,
without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority. Any topping or lopping approved shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard 3998 (Tree Work) or any other BS replacing this.
b.	If any retained tree is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, another tree shall be planted at the same place and that tree shall be of such size and species, and shall be planted at such time, as may be specified in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
c.	The erection of fencing for the protection of any retained tree shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plans and arboricultural report and particulars before any equipment, machinery or materials are brought onto the site for the purposes of the development, and shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site. Nothing shall be stored or placed in any area fenced in accordance with this condition and the ground levels within those areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavation be made, without prior written approval
of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To enable the Local Planning Authority to ensure the protection of retained trees from damage, in the interests of visual amenity

Condition : 40 - Removal of Vegetation	
All removal of trees, hedgerows, shrubs, scrub or tall herbaceous vegetation shall be undertaken between September and February inclusive. If this is not possible, then a suitably qualified ecologist shall check the areas concerned immediately prior to the clearance works to ensure that no nesting or nest-building birds are present. If any nesting birds are present, then the vegetation shall not be removed until the fledglings have left the nest.
Reason: All wild birds, their nests and young are protected during the nesting period under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended). In the interests of nature conservation and biodiversity.

Condition : 41 - Ecological watching Brief	All removal of woodland or scrub shall be carried out in the reptile active season and under an Ecological Watching Brief prepared by a suitably qualified ecologist.

Reason: To ensure reptiles are protected during their hibernation period in the interests of nature conservation and biodiversity
